title: Continual inference reading + experiment scrapbook
content:
Quick context: I want a lightweight, production-friendly approach for long-lived assistant state. Goal: low incremental cost, bounded memory, stable quality across distributions. These are scratchy, non-linear notes — meant to capture ideas for small protos and failing hypotheses.

High-level takeaways from recent reads (week of 2025-09-08):
- Continual retrieval (paper A: arXiv:2508.01234) — shows a small-perf win by time-decayed index + reservoir sampling for user sessions. Nice: memory budget guarantees. Questions: how does decay interact with episodic bursts (e.g., customer support spike)?
- Cache-aware prompting (blog post B) — put a short summary token bag into prompt when the model's KV budget is small. Works when the model can consume short synthetic summaries; less helpful for factual precision.
- Sparse rehearsal via compressed exemplars — keep 50 compressed exemplars per user, update with k-means on embedding space every N sessions. Cheap to store (embedding only). Need to test freshness/obsolescence tradeoff.

Ideas for prototypes:
1) In-memory hybrid: per-user LRU of recent docs (5 items) + global compressed exemplar store (topical clusters). Retrieve by hybrid score: lambda * sim_recent + (1-lambda) * sim_cluster.
   - Hypothesis: combines recency with coverage to avoid catastrophic forgetting of important background facts.
   - Metric: QA accuracy on held-out persona facts; average token cost per session.

2) Prompt compaction service: tiny on-host function that compacts a retrieved chunk to a 64-token summary (via a small quantized model or distilled LM), returns summary for final prompt.
   - Tradeoff: compute cost of compaction vs. token savings. If compaction model is local and quantized, may be cheaper than sending full context to hosted LLM.

3) KV cache patching for long-horizon: store compressed KV deltas per user epoch; on request, restore the relevant deltas into runtime KV cache. Explore sparse activation so we don't blow memory.
   - Implementation sketch: each delta is a set of (layer, head, compressed-kv-vector, timestep-range). Need efficient merging heuristics.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Dimensions: retrieval style (fresh LRU vs decayed reservoir), exemplar compression (none / PCA64 / product-quant 8-bit), compaction (none / 64-token distilled), prompt budget (512 / 1024 tokens), traffic pattern (steady / bursty / drift).
- Key metrics: task utility (F1 on factual QA), hallucination rate (manual label check), end-to-end latency p95, token cost per session, memory per-active-user.

Open questions / failure modes observed in notes:
- Drift: exemplar clusters become stale quickly for users in dynamic domains (news, social). Need recency weighting that beats clustering alone.
- Overfitting: retrieving too-similar exemplars causes model to stick to past phrasing and repeat mistakes. Need diversity penalty.
- Privacy: storing compressed exemplars still risky for sensitive fields; add opt-out and stronger transforms (differentially private summaries?)

Short prompt tests (manual):
- Test case: user earlier taught assistant that "Note A: prefer metric tons". Later assistant should use preferred unit when writing summary. Try retrieval of compressed exemplar containing "prefer metric tons".
  - Prompt template: [system instructions] + [retrieved summaries] + [user message] -> expected: use metric tons. Failure mode: retrieval returns similar context but missing explicit preference.

Notes-to-self:
- Implement small bench harness: python script to spin mini-rag prototype (index = FAISS on 16k dim PCA-reduced embeddings). Use quantized sim search to approximate.
- Measure: for 100 synthetic users, simulate 30 sessions each with drift events at session 10 and 20. Report metrics.
- Keep implementation simple: start with cloud-hosted endpoint (hosted API) + local mini-retriever to simulate private-deploy flow.

Useful links and anchor refs:
- arXiv:2508.01234 — Continual retrieval with reservoir + decay
- mini-rag-proto PR: github.com/redwood-inference/mini-rag-proto/pull/14 (prototype code and simple harness)
- internal note: JIRA-RETRIEVAL-122 (bench task)

Next actions (short list):
- [ ] Draft bench harness by 2025-09-19 (baseline retrieval + exemplar compression)
- [ ] Run drift simulation and collect metrics by 2025-09-26
- [ ] Pair with Aisha on privacy transforms (meeting 2025-09-16 done)
- [ ] If baseline promising, push an internal demo for solutions-engers by 2025-10-05

Random heuristics I'm curious about:
- Keep 2 "gold" exemplars per user (always preserved): these are synthetically generated summaries of user-stated invariants (preferences, role). Update policy: only rewrite when explicit conflict. Might stabilize behavior.
- Use a TTL that is a function of user activity: TTL = base * (1 + log(1 + sessions_past_week)).

Rough resource estimate for a small pilot (5k active users):
- Index storage: ~5k * 50 exemplars * 512 bytes compressed ≈ 128MB (embeds + metadata).
- Compaction compute: assume 10ms per compaction on quantized small model — estimate 5–10 vCPU equivalent at 99th percentile for 1k compactions/min. Needs verification.

End: this is messy — will iterate. If you read this and want to hack, start with the mini-rag-proto PR, play with exemplar compression first, then add compaction. Notes tagged 'todo' above.
